fact: 1904年圣路易斯路易斯安那购地博览会（St. Louis World's Fair）于4月30日开幕、12月1日闭幕；地方、州与联邦资金合计1,500万美元，60多个国家和当时45州中的43州设展位，参观者近1,970万人次。

sources.title: Wikipedia — Louisiana Purchase Exposition
sources.quote: The Louisiana Purchase Exposition, informally known as the St. Louis World's Fair, was an international exposition held in St. Louis, Missouri, United States, from April 30 to December 1, 1904. Local, state, and federal funds totaling $15 million (equivalent to $538 million in 2025) were used to finance the event. More than 60 countries and 43 of the then-45 American states maintained exhibition spaces at the fair, which was attended by nearly 19.7 million people.

sources.title: Final Report of the Louisiana Purchase Exposition Commission（Gutenberg #13266 官方报告）
sources.quote: Including the appropriation made by the act of Congress, the sum of $15,000,000 was provided for the exposition, as follows: Donated by the city of St. Louis ...................... $5,000,000

fact: 1904年圣路易斯奥运会（第三届夏季奥运会）开幕式为5月14日，主要比赛期为7月1日至11月26日，参赛者650人、来自10个当时认可的国家奥委会名单（美国一国即占543人），设95个奖牌项目；日本不在该10个NOC名单之列。

fact: 1904年11月8日大选中，西奥多·罗斯福以336张对140张选举人票击败纽约州上诉法院首席法官Alton B. Parker；民主党全国代表大会于7月6—9日在圣路易斯举行。罗斯福普选票7,630,457（56.4%），Parker为5,083,880（37.6%）。

sources.title: Miller Center — Theodore Roosevelt: Campaigns and Elections
sources.quote: The election, however, had never been in doubt. TR won 336 electoral votes to Parker's 140. He took every state outside of the South, including Missouri. / When the Democrats met in St. Louis, they picked two conservatives, Judge Alton B. Parker, from New York, and eighty-one-year-old Henry G. Davis

sources.title: Wikipedia — 1904 United States presidential election
sources.quote: The Democratic Convention that met in St. Louis on July 6–9, 1904, has been called "one of the most exciting and sensational in the history of the Democratic Party". ... election_date: November 8, 1904 — Roosevelt/Fairbanks: electoral votes 336, popular vote 7,630,457 (56.4%); Parker/Davis: electoral votes 140, popular vote 5,083,880 (37.6%)

fact: 1904年3月14日，美国最高法院以5:4在Northern Securities Co. v. United States（193 U.S. 197）中裁定摩根等组成的北方证券公司铁路合并违反《谢尔曼反托拉斯法》并命令解散该公司；这确立了联邦政府可以解散巨型托拉斯的先例。

sources.title: Wikipedia — Northern Securities Co. v. United States
sources.quote: Northern Securities Co. v. United States, 193 U.S. 197 (1904), was a case heard by the U.S. Supreme Court in December 1903. The Court ruled 5-4 against the stockholders of the Great Northern and Northern Pacific railroad companies, holding that their merger was effectively a monopoly falling within the prohibitions of the Sherman Antitrust Act, and to dissolve the Northern Securities Company. [Decided March 14, 1904]

sources.title: Miller Center — Theodore Roosevelt: Domestic Affairs
sources.quote: In 1904, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in favor of the government and ordered the company dismantled. The high court's action was a major victory for the administration and put the business community on notice

fact: 1903年《海-布诺-瓦里拉条约》使美国以1,000万美元一次性支付加每年25万美元取得对巴拿马运河区的永久控制权；该安排1904年生效执行，运河区成为美国在中美洲的主权飞地与军事 staging 区域。

sources.title: Miller Center — Theodore Roosevelt: Foreign Affairs
sources.quote: In 1903, the Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty with Panama gave the United States perpetual control of the canal for a price of $10 million and an annual payment of $250,000. This project also converted the Panama Canal Zone into a major staging area for American military forces

fact: 圣路易斯世博会官方规则明文规定入场票价为50美分（原文：ARTICLE V. SECTION I. The price of admission will be 50 cents.），这是1904年圣路易斯最基础的公共消费价格锚点。

sources.title: Final Report of the Louisiana Purchase Exposition Commission（Gutenberg #13266）
sources.quote: ARTICLE V. SECTION I. The price of admission will be 50 cents.

fact: 官方最终报告显示博览会全期总入场20,066,537人次，其中付费入场12,804,616人次（约63.8%）；开幕当月至1904年5月免费票约占总入场的三分之二，此后经委员会治理才将免费票压到一半以下。

sources.title: Final Report of the Louisiana Purchase Exposition Commission（Gutenberg #13266）
sources.quote: Total admissions during the entire period of the exposition ....................... 20,066,537 / Total paid admissions during the entire period of the exposition ................ 12,804,616 / On April 30, and during the month of May, 1904, of the 1,841,275 total admissions only 667,772 were paid admissions, thus making the free admissions substantially two-thirds of the total.

fact: 1900年《金本位法》确立的美元含金量在1904年继续有效：美元含23.22格令纯金，约合每盎司黄金20.67美元，美国所有货币须维持与该标准的等值。

sources.title: Gold Standard Act of 1900 法条原文（经 Global Macro Expert 转载）
sources.quote: That the dollar consisting of twenty-five and eight-tenths grains of gold nine-tenths fine, as established by section thirty-five hundred and eleven of the Revised Statutes of the United States, shall be the standard unit of value, and all forms of money issued or coined by the United States shall be maintained at a parity of value with this standard.

sources.title: Peterson Institute — Kirkegaard, The US Gold Standard and the International Monetary System
sources.quote: The Currency Act of 1900, also known as the Gold Standard Act, established an official American mono-metallic gold standard with a dollar worth 23.22 grains of pure gold.

sources.title: World Gold Council — Gold Standard Act, 1900
sources.quote: United States notes became redeemable for gold at the historical rate of $20.67 per ounce.

fact: 美国钢铁公司（U.S. Steel）由J.P.摩根于1901年3月2日整合卡内基钢铁、联邦钢铁与国民钢铁而成，合并金额4.92亿美元，是当时唯一十亿美元级企业；其股份自1901年起在纽约证券交易所挂牌（普通股代码X），1904年属于少数可公开买卖的巨型工业企业股票之一。

sources.title: Wikipedia — U.S. Steel
sources.quote: In 1901, J. P. Morgan created U.S. Steel by merging Carnegie Steel Company, Federal Steel, and National Steel for $492 million (equivalent to roughly $19 billion in 2025). [公司信息框：Founded March 2, 1901；Traded as NYSE : X (1901–2025)]

fact: 1904年美国电影仍在窥镜式单人机与杂耍厅穿插放映阶段：1905年6月19日匹兹堡Smithfield Street开出首家5美分票价的Nickelodeon店面影院后，影院数量在1907—1908年间翻倍至约8,000家，估计1910年每周吸引最多2,600万美国人观影——1904年底至1905年存在开店与供片的先发窗口。

sources.title: Wikipedia — Nickelodeon (movie theater)（引 Bowser 1990、Aronson 2008 等）
sources.quote: The earliest films had been shown in 'peep show' machines or projected in vaudeville theaters as one of the otherwise live acts. ... On June 19, 1905, they opened a small storefront theater with the name on Smithfield Street in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. ... Statistics at the time show that the number of nickelodeons in the United States doubled between 1907 and 1908 to around 8,000, and it was estimated that by 1910 as many as 26 million Americans visited these theaters weekly.

sources.title: Library of Congress — History of Edison Motion Pictures: Fictional Films Dominate（引 Bowser）
sources.quote: by 1908, there were approximately 8,000 nickelodeons in the U.S. The theaters attracted a wide clientele ... Appearing first in 1905, nickelodeons featured movie shows all day long

fact: 纽约州在圣路易斯世博会的展品清单包括由州监狱部门承办的“Bertillon体系与指纹识别系统展览”（EXHIBIT OF BERTILLON AND FINGER PRINT SYSTEMS OF IDENTIFICATIONS）以及矿山与冶金展览——人体测量与指纹识别作为最新身份识别技术在1904年被官方展示推广。

fact: 1904年8月30日15时于华盛顿大学Francis Field起跑的奥运会马拉松全程40公里，在约32°C高温与扬尘土路上进行，全程仅12英里处一口井一个补水点；选手William Garcia因高温、尘土与缺水被迫退赛并住院数日、一度生命垂危。

sources.title: Olympedia — Marathon, Men (1904)
sources.quote: The race was 40 km and was held on a 90° F (32° C) day. In addition, it was run over dusty country roads, and the lead automobiles kicked up so much dust that the runners practically choked on it throughout the race. There was also only one water stop on the course, that being a well at 12 miles. / Garcia would eventually drop out, and suffered so badly from the heat, dust, and lack of water, that he spent several days in the hospital, his life in the balance, before recovering.

fact: 1904年奥运会马拉松于8月30日举行，32名选手起跑：Tom Hicks以3:28:53获金牌，途中被教练喂食硫酸士的宁（蛋清送服）与白兰地；率先冲入体育场的Fred Lorz实为中途搭车，被揭穿后遭终身禁赛（后解除，1905年仍赢得波士顿马拉松）。

sources.title: Olympedia — Marathon, Men (1904)
sources.quote: 1 20 Tom Hicks USA 3-28:53 ... Gold 2 7 Albert Corey USA 3-34:52 Silver 3 12 Arthur Newton USA 3-47:33 Bronze / He was then passed by Fred Lorz, who was refreshed after having ridden in an automobile most of the race. ... Lorz entered the stadium first and received the crowd's plaudits, as they were oblivious to his scheme. ... Lorz was soon found out and was banned from amateur competition for life, only to see it rescinded in time for him to win the 1905 Boston Marathon. / His handlers helped him, administering strychnine sulfate in an egg white, giving him water, and sponging him down. ... fact: 1904年8月31日400米栏比赛中，George Poage获铜牌，被Olympedia记述为“首位获得个人奥运奖牌的黑人运动员”——种族隔离时代的奥运领奖台突破。

sources.title: Olympedia — 400 metres Hurdles, Men (1904)
sources.quote: In third place, George Poage won what is usually described as the first Olympic medal ever won by a black man. In 1900, a black man had competed in the tug-of-war for France, winning a silver medal. However, Poage's bronze was the first individual Olympic medal won by a Black athlete.

fact: 世博会特许经营（concessions）是真实可查的盈利部门：官方账目记载“Pike”游乐区租金收入218,187.50美元、博览会期间特许经营收入2,812,995.59美元；场地另有逾50项“Pike”特许娱乐项目。特许申请须在1902年12月1日前提出并提供保证金。

fact: 吉列（Gillette）在1904年专利有效期内的实际定价为：5美元买剃刀加12片刀片、每 additional 12片刀片1美元，并维持较高刀架价格；流行叙事中“1904年起低价或免费赠送刀架以销售刀片”与现有证据不符。

sources.title: The Razors-and-Blades Myth(s), Randal C. Picker
sources.quote: By mid-1904, it had settled on the business model and prices that it would use over the life of the 1904 patents: $5 for a razor with a pack of 12 blades and additional packs of 12 blades for $1. Gillette maintained a high price throughout the life of the patents, and it was only as the patents were ready to expire that Gillette switched strategies.
